Panegyric

pan-uh-JIR-ik · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Panegyric is a formal or elaborate speech or piece of writing praising someone.

At the retirement dinner, the CEO's oldest friend delivered a panegyric that traced forty years of her career, calling her a legend of the entire industry.

Worked Example

The eulogy quickly turned into a panegyric, with speaker after speaker praising the senator's decades of public service in increasingly glowing terms.

A panegyric isn't just a nice compliment -- it's an entire formal speech built around celebrating someone's achievements.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

tribute: a public expression of respect or gratitude

eulogy: a speech praising someone, often at a funeral (a word you met earlier in this course)

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

diatribe: a forceful, bitter verbal attack

condemnation: strong public criticism

Where it sits · how lavish the praise becomes — compliment → panegyric → adulation

compliment vs. panegyric: A compliment is a brief, casual bit of praise, much lower-key than a full formal speech.

adulation vs. panegyric: Adulation is excessive, almost worshipful praise, even more over-the-top than a panegyric.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pan-

prefix — pan-: all, every (Greek)

root — -egyric

root — -egyric: of a public assembly (Greek agora, 'assembly')

Put it together

Put it together: Panegyric comes from Greek pan- ('all') + a root meaning 'public assembly' -- literally a speech delivered before an entire gathered assembly, which is exactly what a panegyric still is: a formal speech praising someone in public.

Use the root in a new word: agoraphobia

Use the root in a new word: agoraphobia: Agoraphobia, the fear of open and crowded public places, is built on Greek agora, 'the assembly place' -- the same root, in its dialect form agyris, hiding inside panegyric.

Word Choice

Panegyric is a formal, almost ceremonial word -- reach for it when describing an entire speech or piece of writing built around praise, not just a passing compliment.
